paths.description: Homepage: entry, search/navigation, promotional content, consent and personalization chrome.
Department landing: representative catalogue/category archetype and mobile reflow.
Search results: representative product-discovery listing for “iphone”.
Product detail: pricing, metadata, add-to-cart action, long-page layout, and no-JS content.
Empty cart: shopping continuity and recovery/recommendation state.
Authentication: form semantics, invalid submission, autofill, and modern authentication.
Invalid route: HTTP/error-state clarity and recovery.

findings.summary: The site stays light when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the preference probe reports body background rgb(245,245,245), color-scheme normal, and no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS/API marker inspection found zero view-transition rules, while navigation uses conventional cross-document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document transitions for high-value state changes and opt eligible cross-document routes into View Transitions with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages do not expose scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The 5,797px homepage and 17,898px product page have static multi-row headers; source markers show no scroll-state or scroll-driven navigation technique.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-state container queries or a lightweight shrinking header/progress treatment for long catalogue and product pages.

findings.summary: The account prompt is custom-positioned rather than anchor-positioned.
findings.evidence: The load screenshot shows an account tooltip attached to the header icon, but rendered CSS contains no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try markers.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement transient header prompts as a popover anchored to the account control with position-try fallbacks.

findings.summary: Two simultaneous load-time interruptions obscure the primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop load shows a large cookie banner covering the hero while an account sign-in prompt covers the navigation and hero; mobile shows the cookie panel covering product cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay nonessential account promotion, keep consent compact, and ensure every interruption is independently dismissible without covering the primary task.

findings.summary: Visible overlays are built without semantic dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe counted zero dialog, popover, and details elements despite visible cookie and account overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover with declarative light-dismiss for the account prompt; preserve focus and Escape behavior.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome crowds the first viewport.
findings.evidence: The desktop first viewport contains an app-install strip, two navigation rows, an account prompt, a hero promotion, cookie controls, and an accessibility widget; little unobstructed shopping content remains.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary promotion, remove automatic account prompting, and reserve the first viewport for search, navigation, and current content.

findings.summary: Representative catalogue and product pages overflow on mobile.
findings.evidence: At 360px, layout reports 840px horizontal overflow on the category route (1,200px layout viewport) and 27px on the product route; the homepage itself has none.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop widths, use intrinsic grids and minmax(), and verify every archetype at 320–360px.

findings.summary: Shared catalogue components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The category route forces a 1,200px layout at a 360px visual viewport, and rendered styles expose no @container rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable listing shells and container-query card/filter/header layouts rather than relying only on desktop viewport rules.

findings.summary: The not-found route does not explain the failure or offer recovery.
findings.evidence: The deliberately invalid route renders a mostly blank carousel shell with arrows and dots, no 404 message, no search prompt, and no route recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an explicit 404 state with a clear message, search, home/category links, and a correct non-2xx status.

findings.summary: Throttled mobile loading misses the LCP target.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance is 0.62 with FCP 4.4s and LCP 10.3s; an unthrottled trace is faster at LCP 1.36s, showing network/CPU conditions are the risk rather than instability.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce critical request chains and initial script work, and validate against mobile Lighthouse and field data.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavier and less direct than necessary.
findings.evidence: HAR records 82 requests and 1,847,353 transferred bytes; Lighthouse flags LCP discovery and network dependency tree insights.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the LCP image explicit priority, shorten blocking chains, self-host or streamline fonts, and set effective caching for static resources.

findings.summary: The initial route ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 288,526 bytes of unused JavaScript and 63,583 bytes of unused CSS; HAR attributes 653,632 transferred bytes to scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split homepage-only features, delay analytics and nonessential widgets, and remove unused CSS from the critical route.

findings.summary: Some controls and fields lack robust accessible naming.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails label-content-name-mismatch; the homepage probe estimates 34 unnamed interactive elements and the login email input has no associated label or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Use visible associated labels and make each accessible name contain its visible label; audit icon-only controls with axe and a keyboard/screen-reader pass.

findings.summary: Several text/UI combinations fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three color-contrast failures on the homepage. Forced-colors remains usable, but that does not repair default-theme WCAG contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG AA and regression-test default, hover, disabled, and promotional states.

findings.summary: The homepage heading/landmark structure starts without a page-level heading.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe finds no h1 and no header landmark; content begins with many h2 product titles. Visible focus does work on the tested link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1 and a semantic header; retain the visible focus treatment and verify a logical keyboard order.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow fails on key catalogue routes.
findings.evidence: The 360px category and product tests report horizontal overflow of 840px and 27px respectively despite a scalable viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Rebuild fixed-width sections with intrinsic responsive sizing and test reflow at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Image markup omits dimensions and often delivers unsuitable assets.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 51 of 54 images without width/height, 19 oversized, and 46 legacy-format images. CLS happened to remain low in this capture but reservation is not guaranteed.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, provide responsive sources, and prefer AVIF/WebP where suitable.

findings.summary: The homepage cannot use the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons, including cache-control:no-store on the main resource and a JavaScript request.
findings.suggestedFix: Restrict no-store to truly sensitive responses and avoid mutating HTTP-only cookie state on ordinary catalogue navigation.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable and one public archetype is not mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors; probes find 25 javascript/no-href links on home and 7 javascript links on category. The category route also forces a 1,200px layout at 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and correct the category responsive layout while retaining the valid viewport meta tag.

findings.summary: Robots and sitemap endpoints return 410 Gone.
findings.evidence: Direct requests to /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml both returned HTTP 410 with the same 587-byte generic Gone page, even though canonical tags and public pages return 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid robots.txt and sitemap index with 200 responses, reference the sitemap from robots.txt, and monitor accidental indexing-policy regressions.

findings.summary: Cookie transport attributes and CSP are weaker than the HTTPS transport.
findings.evidence: The page is HTTPS with HSTS, but all 14 observed first-party cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark HTTPS cookies Secure, choose Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is required, and migrate to a nonce/hash CSP that removes unsafe-eval and unsafe-inline.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party activity starts on the initial page load.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture sees 9 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and Sentry, while the cookie decision panel is still visible in the load screenshots.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential analytics behind consent, minimise identifiers and retention, batch events, and document each third party’s purpose.

findings.summary: The relevant sign-in route exposes no phishing-resistant sign-in option.
findings.evidence: The login probe finds only email plus Facebook/Google/Apple controls and zero passkey/WebAuthn markers; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside federated/email recovery, with conditional UI where supported.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Permissions-Policy is missing, Referrer-Policy is the legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade value, and CSP is wildcard-based with unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, although HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN and frame-ancestors are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and a source-restricted CSP.

findings.summary: The app-like commerce experience has no install or offline foundation.
findings.evidence: The homepage promotes a mobile app, but the PWA probe finds no manifest and no service-worker registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a web app manifest and a small service worker that provides a branded offline fallback and safe retry for read-only catalogue routes.

findings.summary: Failure handling can collapse into an unexplained shell.
findings.evidence: The invalid-route capture shows only empty carousel chrome and no useful status or recovery controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Render explicit HTTP/network error components with retry, search, back and home actions, preserving the requested context.

findings.summary: Login validation relies on an unlabeled native error in the wrong language.
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty Romanian login form focuses the field but yields browser text “Please fill in this field”, no aria-invalid, and no role=alert/error message.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a visible Romanian label and post-interaction error, synchronise aria-invalid, and announce the error in a live region.

findings.summary: Sign-in and newsletter fields omit useful autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The login email field has an empty autocomplete value; homepage name/email newsletter inputs also have no autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username or email on sign-in and name/email tokens on newsletter fields; keep autofill styling legible.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 19 oversized assets, 28 without srcset, 46 legacy-format images, and only 7 modern-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP variants, provide srcset/sizes, and match requested dimensions to rendered size.

findings.summary: Initial loading includes avoidable code and background services.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 1.85MB across 82 requests and Lighthouse estimates 288KB unused JavaScript while tracker/Sentry requests start during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay nonessential analytics, error monitoring extras, recommendations, and below-fold code until consent, idle time, or user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party and image costs are high for the first shopping view.
findings.evidence: Nine third-party origins are contacted and images account for 888,969 transferred bytes before the user interacts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route budget for third-party requests and image bytes, defer nonessential origins, and enforce it in performance monitoring.

taskList.title: Repair category/product mobile reflow with intrinsic and container-responsive layouts
Restore robots.txt and sitemap.xml with correct 200 indexing signals
Harden cookie attributes, CSP, Permissions-Policy and Referrer-Policy
Reduce LCP and initial payload by prioritising the hero and removing unused code
Replace simultaneous load-time overlays with semantic, dismissible primitives
Fix labels, accessible names, heading structure, contrast and localized errors
Optimise and responsively deliver images with dimensions and modern formats
Gate and minimise third-party analytics until consent
Add passkeys and correct autofill tokens to sign-in
Add manifest and offline fallback for the app-like commerce shell
